points.quote: If you use a GenAI tool as part of your learning or assessment, you must clearly state this on your work.
points.gist: Students must clearly state on their work if they used a GenAI tool in learning or assessment.

points.quote: Describing how you used it, on a cover sheet or reflective note, and
points.gist: Disclosure may involve describing use on a cover sheet or reflective note.

points.quote: Unless your assignment brief tells you otherwise, you can use AI to:
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Unless the assignment brief says otherwise, students can use AI for a listed set of purposes.

points.quote: Review and summarise your own notes or those generated in group work or discussion (with consent from your fellow participants)
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Students can use AI to review and summarise their own or group notes, with fellow participants' consent.

points.quote: Translating the majority of your own work into English (Principle 4)
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Translating the majority of your own work into English is a prohibited use of AI.

points.quote: Fabricating empirical data to use in a research project or other assessment (Principles 2 and 3)
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Fabricating empirical data for research or other assessment is prohibited.

points.quote: Uploading participant data or responses into GenAI without the participants' consent or ethical approval (Principle 6)
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Uploading participant data or responses to GenAI without consent or ethical approval is prohibited.

points.quote: Submitting GenAI generated content without citation of the AI tool or evidence of how you used it (Principles 1 and 2)
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Submitting GenAI content without citing the tool or evidence of use is prohibited and breaches academic integrity policy.

points.quote: I have saved copies of GenAI outputs used in preparing my assessment. I know I may be asked to provide these as an appendix to my assessment or as part of any misconduct process.
points.gist: The checklist has students save copies of GenAI outputs, which may be requested as an appendix or in a misconduct process.

points.quote: I have not entered into GenAI tools any works that are copyright or the intellectual property of a third party.
points.gist: The checklist asks students to confirm they have not entered third-party copyright or intellectual property works into GenAI tools.

points.quote: Not all GenAI tools are free or accessible. You will not be expected to use paid AI tools.
points.gist: Not all GenAI tools are free or accessible, and students will not be expected to use paid AI tools.

points.quote: Some students may have AI tools provided as part of reasonable adjustments, and we have additional guidance to help you decide whether and how to use AI: Using AI as Assistive Technology.
points.anchor: What you could or should not use AI for in assessed work
points.gist: Some students may have AI tools provided as reasonable adjustments, and additional guidance on Using AI as Assistive Technology exists.

points.quote: Sharing personal information of other people without their consent could be a breach of General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR).
points.gist: Sharing other people's personal information without consent could breach GDPR.

points.quote: Whether malicious or accidental, use of any technology that breaches Academic Integrity can result in you being investigated for academic misconduct.
points.gist: Breaching academic integrity with any technology, maliciously or accidentally, can lead to an academic misconduct investigation.

points.quote: Cite Them Right - alongside citing your sources of research, you are expected to follow the same format for citing your use of AI tools.
points.gist: Students are expected to cite their use of AI tools in the same format used for research sources, via Cite Them Right.
